# Eagle Asset Library

The Eagle plugin connects your desktop Eagle library to the site's asset panel. The browser does not access Eagle directly: all read, search, download, and write requests go through the site backend, which contacts the Eagle Local API address configured by an administrator.

## Before you start

1. Install and start the Eagle desktop app, and open the library you want to use.
2. Make sure the Eagle Local API is available. Its default address is `{{v0}}`.
3. Open plugin settings as an administrator, enter the Base URL, and load the folders.
4. Save the configuration, then choose Eagle as the source in the asset library to browse and import assets.

> Keep Eagle running. Closing the app, switching libraries, or changing the local API port can cause connection failures. These must be reported, rather than hidden as an empty list.

## Site backend endpoints

| Action | Site endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read library | `GET /api/plugins/eagle/library?baseUrl=...` | Get the Eagle version, library name, and folder tree |
| List assets | `GET /api/plugins/eagle/items` | Read assets by folder, keyword, and pagination |
| Thumbnail | `GET /api/plugins/eagle/items/{id}/thumbnail` | Proxy Eagle thumbnails |
| Original file | `GET /api/plugins/eagle/items/{id}/file` | Download and import into site resource storage |
| Write asset | `POST /api/plugins/eagle/items?baseUrl=...` | Write images, videos, or audio back to Eagle |
| Create folder | `POST /api/plugins/eagle/folders?baseUrl=...` | Create an Eagle folder |

These are internal site APIs that require a signed in session and Cookie authentication. Do not call them as if they were official Eagle endpoints.

## Browsing and search

The plugin reads Eagle's folder tree and builds full hierarchical paths. Asset listing supports `folderId`, `keyword`, `limit`, and `offset`. Folders are cached within the current plugin instance; creating a folder invalidates the cache and reloads it. Reopen plugin settings to confirm the folders after switching Eagle libraries.

## Importing into the site

The backend proxies the download of the original Eagle file, then the frontend writes it to the site's own image or media storage. Images retain detected dimensions and MIME types. Videos, audio, and other model files retain their byte size, extension, Eagle item ID, folder, and source metadata.

| Eagle content | Site result | Current limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image | Image asset | Uses the original, not the thumbnail |
| Video | Video asset | Missing dimensions use a 1280×720 display fallback; the original file is unchanged |
| Audio | Audio asset | Duration is determined by browser media inspection |
| Other file | Model asset | Stored as a file resource only |
| Text / entity | Unsupported | Import returns an explicit error |

## Writing back to Eagle

The plugin can convert site images, videos, or audio to data URLs and add them to Eagle. It reads a local Blob first when available; remote generation URLs are downloaded only when no local copy exists. A manually uploaded file must be at most 96 MB, with a MIME type beginning with `image/`, `video/`, or `audio/`.

With automatic upload of generated results enabled, generated assets can be written to the configured target folder. A failed writeback must be reported as such; saving to the site does not mean it was saved to Eagle.

## Configuration fields

| Field | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | Eagle Local API address; must be an explicit HTTP(S) address | `{{v1}}` |
| `autoUploadGenerated` | Automatically write supported generation results to Eagle | On |
| `generatedFolderId` | Target folder ID for automatic writeback | Empty; uses Eagle's default location |

## Security boundaries

- Eagle usually runs locally. The backend must continue validating private network targets and allow only local services explicitly configured by an administrator. This proxy must not become an arbitrary URL fetcher.
- `baseUrl` stores only the service address, without tokens, cookies, or query string keys.
- Original files and data URLs must not enter logs, localStorage, or error reports.
- In a deployment with multiple users, the server's `127.0.0.1` refers to the server itself, not the visitor's computer. Use a connection method supported by Eagle; do not imply that a direct connection is available.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Cannot read the library | Whether Eagle is running, the Base URL and port, and whether the backend can reach the host |
| Empty folders | The library open in Eagle, active filters, and folder hierarchy |
| Thumbnail works but import fails | Whether the original file still exists, file permissions, and backend response status |
| Writeback fails | File size and MIME type, target folder existence, and whether the remote generation link expired |
| A deployed server cannot reach local Eagle | The network topology does not support it; a local bridge is needed, rather than a different frontend URL |

## Official resources

- [Eagle API Documentation](https://api.eagle.cool/)
- [Eagle website and downloads](https://eagle.cool/)

mediaConversion.mediaConversionNodeConnectAnImageToAConv:
# Media conversion node

Connect an image to a conversion node to choose grayscale, Canny edges, AI line art, depth maps, or pose skeletons. AI line art uses the local ControlNet Aux preprocessing model; depth maps use the installed Depth Anything V2 Small model; pose skeletons use ControlNet Aux's OpenPose human preprocessing model. None of these operations loads a Stable Diffusion repainting pipeline. Pose conversion draws human skeletons only and skips images with no detected person with a notice. Video conversion and transparent cutout models are still being validated and are currently marked unavailable.

This plugin reads only the current node's media input and saves results to the node's local asset storage.
